answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the tundra checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The voyage graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the pigment audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 2 times its size, so a group of 93 keys loses far more than 93 single identities would. That is 30 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
